Chapter 1: Introduction, Purpose, and Taxonomy

Introduction, Purpose, and Taxonomy

NewAgent is engineered from the ground up as a high-performance, asynchronous terminal-first AI agent client. Built specifically to operate under the austere hardware and network constraints typical of mobile environments like Android running Termux alongside standard Linux distributions, it eschews bloated web frameworks in favor of direct, low-latency process control. Its foundational purpose is to bridge the gap between high-level language model reasoning and deterministic, local execution, enabling a language model to read user requests, parse structured action primitives, and execute them safely within a guarded local environment.

Unlike contemporary agentic frameworks that rely on heavy, opaque runtime abstractions and unstructured plain-text memory, NewAgent roots all configuration, state persistence, and inter-process communication in the Boehen Elton JSON (BEJSON) standard and Multi-File Database (MFDB) structures. This design decision ensures that every operational parameter, session history, key ledger, and knowledge pool entry adheres to a strict relational schema with verifiable data types and structural integrity.

Operational Classification and Architecture Taxonomy

NewAgent occupies a unique category within the ecosystem of developer-focused AI tools: it is a dual-engine, state-managed agentic shell. Rather than locking the operator into a single proprietary execution paradigm, its core engine dynamically bridges a REST-based custom action tag system with a native tool-calling interactions engine. The system taxonomy is organized into distinct, modular functional layers as detailed below:

Layer Primary Components Operational Purpose
Entry Points agent.py, cliagent.py, webagent.py Exposes interactive TUI, headless scripting, and token-gated local web terminal interfaces sharing a unified backend.
Engine Core engine_rest.py, engine_interactions.py Manages asynchronous model prompting, multi-key SHA-256 ledger rotation, and fallback execution handling.
State & Storage BEJSON 104/104a/104db, MFDB Enforces strict positional integrity, atomic file writes, and zero data drift across configuration registries.

Core Philosophy and Positioning

The core philosophy governing NewAgent is absolute operator autonomy combined with extreme defensive hardening. Contemporary agentic frameworks frequently abstract away file system interactions, shell executions, and API key management, exposing operators to silent failures, rate-limit lockouts, and prompt injection vulnerabilities. NewAgent reverses this by enforcing total transparency:

  • Deterministic State: Every session maintains explicit transactional boundaries through BEJSON schemas, avoiding hidden state mutations.
  • Resilient Fault Tolerance: Network failures, token exhaustion, and API rate limits trigger automatic backoff protocols, circuit breakers, and key rotation routines without dropping the active session.
  • Modular Extensibility: Companion tools like NA-CMS, NA-WebToolkit, and the sub-agent administrative suite do not operate as disconnected utilities; they inherit the exact same core libraries, path guards, and execution sandboxes as the primary terminal client.

By coupling an uncompromised terminal-first user experience with rigorous data structuring standards, NewAgent establishes a predictable, highly auditable environment for autonomous task execution and code maintenance.

Chapter 2: Technical Architecture and Dual Engine Mechanics

Technical Architecture and Dual Engine Mechanics

NewAgent's underlying architecture is built around an asynchronous event loop management core that decouples interface inputs from long-running execution chains. Whether driven through the interactive terminal client (agent.py), the headless script executor (cliagent.py), or the Flask-backed local web wrapper (webagent.py), the system relies on a unified asynchronous dispatch model. In webagent.py, this infrastructure is further optimized via a persistent background event loop running in a daemon thread, paired with a thread-safe execution helper (run_async()) that utilizes run_coroutine_threadsafe(). This eliminates the catastrophic overhead and platform-specific limitations of instantiating fresh event loops per HTTP request.

The Dual-Engine Paradigm: REST Tag Parsing vs. Native Tool Calling

At the center of NewAgent's processing model lies a dynamic engine switch allowing operators to toggle between two distinct prompting and execution strategies: the custom-tag REST engine and the native tool-calling Interactions engine.

Engine Mode Primary Module Execution Mechanism
REST lib_bejson_newagent_engine_rest.py Parses XML-style action tags (e.g., <exec>, <read_file>) from model prose, executing them via a guarded queue dispatcher.
Interactions lib_bejson_newagent_engine_interactions.py Utilizes native provider tool declarations, executing mapped Python functions (do_map) inline per turn.

The REST engine (RestPrompter) relies on rigorous prompt engineering combined with explicit tag parsing (actions.parse_actions()). When a model returns structured action tags within its response, actions.run_action_queue() evaluates each primitive against a path guard and an execution denylist before dispatching them. Conversely, the Interactions engine maps native tool schemas directly to Python callables in a structured dispatch dictionary (do_map), enabling tight integration with models that support native function declaration protocols.

Asynchronous Loop Management and Signal Safety

Process termination and interrupt handling require strict determinism to prevent state corruption across BEJSON registries and active session transcripts. NewAgent replaces raw, unsafe signal handlers with cooperative event-loop task cancellation. Within agent.py, operating system signals such as SIGTERM are intercepted by the running event loop via loop.add_signal_handler() rather than raw C-level callbacks:

loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
main_task = asyncio.current_task()
try:
    loop.add_signal_handler(signal.SIGTERM, main_task.cancel)
except NotImplementedError:
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda signum, frame: main_task.cancel())

By mapping termination signals to asyncio.CancelledError, the runtime ensures that active coroutines hit predictable cooperative cancellation points. This prevents mid-execution interruptions inside file I/O operations or atomic BEJSON serialization blocks, leaving the final completed turn's resume state fully intact on disk.

Circuit-Breaker Fault Tolerance and Exponential Backoff

Network instability, rate-limit enforcement (HTTP 429), and upstream provider errors are inevitable when operating across constrained mobile links or public API endpoints. NewAgent hardens its execution loop through a multi-tier fault tolerance strategy:

  • Circuit Breaker: The main event loop tracks consecutive turn failures (_consecutive_turn_failures). If failures reach the hardcoded threshold (_max_consecutive_turn_failures = 3), the circuit breaker trips, snapshotting a final emergency backup to the backups/ directory and terminating the process to protect corrupted state.
  • Stateful Recovery: Upon encountering a recoverable API or transport error, the orchestrator instantly drops and rebuilds the prompter instance, preventing a single poisoned connection or malformed response object from corrupting subsequent turns.
  • Exponential Backoff and Jitter: Network communication modules implement rigorous retry jitter policies to prevent thundering-herd rate-limit spikes when rotating through exhausted API key pools.

This fault-tolerant design ensures that transient network drops result in clean, automated retries or graceful degradation rather than silent data loss or unhandled interpreter crashes.

Chapter 3: BEJSON Data Architecture and State Persistence

BEJSON Data Architecture and State Persistence

State persistence in NewAgent relies entirely on the Boehnen Elton JSON (BEJSON) standard and the Multi-File Database (MFDB) paradigm. Eschewing unstructured configuration text files, SQLite binaries, or proprietary NoSQL formats, BEJSON provides a strict, human-readable structural schema for every configuration setting, session ledger, model catalog, and registry. This architecture guarantees absolute predictability across varied execution environments, from local desktop Linux deployments to constrained Android/Termux mobile terminals.

The BEJSON Format Ecosystem: 104, 104a, and 104db

The BEJSON standard implements three distinct formatting specifications tailored to specific relational and document storage requirements:

Format Schema Structural Purpose Key Characteristics
104 General document and single-table storage Standard tabular schema mapping fields to array values without complex hierarchy constraints.
104a Enhanced application configuration and single-project chunks Enforces strict scalar types (string, integer, boolean, number), prohibiting nested arrays or objects within primary value arrays.
104db Multi-table relational packaging (MFDB) Stapled multi-table schema requiring a mandatory Record_Type_Parent discriminator as field index zero.

Format 104a governs core configuration documents such as config.json and constant_config.bejson. Type declarations within the schema's Fields array are rigorously checked against a canonical vocabulary (string, integer, number, boolean, array, object). Ambiguous types like any are strictly rejected by the validator to prevent runtime parsing drift.

The Field Map Cache and Positional Integrity

While BEJSON documents store records as dense, space-efficient positional arrays (Values), application code never relies on hardcoded array indices. Accessing column data positionally (e.g., row[1]) creates a catastrophic vulnerability to schema evolution; if an upstream package inserts a new field at index zero, every downstream positional read silently corrupts state data.

To eliminate this hazard, NewAgent mandates the use of the Field Map Cache via bejson_core_get_field_map(). When loading any BEJSON document, the core parser builds an O(1) name-to-index mapping dictionary derived directly from the document's own Fields declaration:

def _doc_to_job_dict(doc: dict) -> dict:
    fmap = bejson_core_get_field_map(doc)
    tasks = []
    for row in doc.get("Values", []):
        def get(field, default=""):
            idx = fmap.get(field)
            if idx is None:
                raise KeyError(f"Field map miss: '{field}' missing from document schema.")
            return row[idx] if idx < len(row) else default
        tasks.append({
            "task_name": get("task_name", ""),
            "task_completed": bool(get("task_completed", False)),
        })
    return tasks

By enforcing strict field-name resolution through the cached map and raising explicit exceptions on map misses rather than falling back to silent guesses, the architecture ensures absolute forward and backward compatibility across schema updates.

Atomic Writing Guarantees and MFDB Storage

Data corruption resulting from interrupted writes—whether caused by low-memory operating system kills on mobile devices or sudden power loss—is prevented through strict atomic writing protocols. BEJSON and MFDB write operations never write directly to live configuration files or database manifests. Instead, updates follow a precise atomic sequence:

  1. Serializing the target document into a valid JSON/BEJSON string payload.
  2. Writing the payload to a temporary sibling file (e.g., config.json.tmp) within the same directory partition.
  3. Invoking operating system-level atomic file replacement (os.replace() or POSIX equivalent) to swap the temporary file into the final destination path instantaneously.

In the Multi-File Database (MFDB) architecture, this atomic persistence model is extended to multi-entity deployments. A central manifest file (104a.mfdb.bejson) acts as a card catalog mapping entity names to their respective storage files, while individual entity records are appended or updated atomically. This prevents partial writes, ensuring that state files remain pristine and fully validated at every lifecycle stage.

Chapter 4: Token Efficiency and Memory Optimization

Token Efficiency and Memory Optimization

Operating an asynchronous agent client on constrained hardware—such as Android/Termux mobile environments or resource-limited edge nodes—requires obsessive management of system memory and API token consumption. Unconstrained prompt assembly or unbounded transcript growth leads immediately to context bloat, sluggish inference latency, and rapid financial exhaustion of LLM API budgets. NewAgent solves this through a rigorous token optimization pipeline comprising dynamic context budgeting, the Context Bubble assembly engine, mtime-cached static file reading, and automated conversational history trimming.

The Context Bubble Assembly Mechanism

Rather than dumping an entire codebase or static instruction set into every model prompt, NewAgent constructs a modular, budget-capped payload known as the Context Bubble. Managed via lib_bejson_newagent_context_bubble.py, the bubble assembles per-turn context dynamically by concatenating prioritized sections against strict token limits:

Context Component Source File / Origin Priority & Budget Rule
Persistent Policy Context/Persistent_Policy.md Mandatory preamble; injected unconditionally at the apex of every turn.
Active Tasks checklist_*.bejson Injected automatically if incomplete checklist items exist in the working directory.
Environment Sourcing .env/secure/ & .env/user/ Budget-capped drip merging configuration variables and runtime environment paths.
Directory Context context.bejson (Root-to-Leaf) Walks filesystem ancestry; nearer directory sections replace broader ancestor rules.
Keyword Knowledge knowledge_pool.bejson Weight-biased round-robin rotation triggered by substring matching on user messages.

By compartmentalizing these data sources and enforcing strict character-to-token budget ratios, the Context Bubble ensures that the model receives precisely the tactical information required for the current turn without inflating the prompt payload with redundant state.

Mtime-Cached Static File Reading

A major bottleneck in naive agent architectures is the repetitive disk I/O and parsing overhead incurred when reading multi-kilobyte static policy documents, constant registries, and knowledge pools on every single conversational turn. NewAgent eliminates this overhead through an optimized, mtime- and size-keyed caching wrapper (_cached_read()).

_FILE_CACHE: dict[str, tuple[float, int, str]] = {}

def _cached_read(file_path: Path) -> str:
    """Read a static file only if its modification time or size has changed."""
    stat = file_path.stat()
    mtime, size = stat.st_mtime, stat.st_size
    cache_key = str(file_path.resolve())
    
    if cache_key in _FILE_CACHE:
        cached_mtime, cached_size, cached_content = _FILE_CACHE[cache_key]
        if cached_mtime == mtime and cached_size == size:
            return cached_content
            
    content = file_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    _FILE_CACHE[cache_key] = (mtime, size, content)
    return content

This caching layer guarantees that static knowledge files (spanning ~35KB of text across policy, triggers, and constants) are parsed from disk exactly once. Subsequent turns inspect filesystem metadata instantly, reducing turn assembly latency to near zero unless an administrator explicitly updates the underlying source documents.

Automated History Trimming and Amnesia Management

Conversational transcripts grow linearly with every user prompt and tool output execution. Left unmitigated, this expansion eventually breaches model token thresholds, causing API rejections or severe degradation in attention accuracy. NewAgent enforces proactive history management via trim_history():

def trim_history(history: list[dict], max_turns: int) -> None:
    """Trim conversational history to enforce maximum turn limits."""
    max_messages = max_turns * 2
    if len(history) > max_messages:
        del history[:-max_messages]

Invoked at the conclusion of every completed turn across agent.py, cliagent.py, and webagent.py, history trimming guarantees that the active prompt payload remains bounded. When long-running sessions demand deep memory compression without retaining raw transcripts, the integrated /amnesia and /rebirth commands condense entire conversation histories into concise, structured recaps, purging bloated token states while preserving operational continuity.

Chapter 5: Positional Integrity and Deterministic Execution

Positional Integrity and Deterministic Execution

The reliability of NewAgent’s state management hinges entirely on the principle of Positional Integrity. In many lightweight database implementations, developers treat data arrays as generic blobs, fetching fields via raw numeric indexes (e.g., row[2]). This is a fatal anti-pattern. In a multi-file database (MFDB) environment where schemas evolve, fields are added, or records are re-ordered, hardcoded positional indexing introduces silent data corruption. NewAgent mandates that all field access must be mediated through the Field Map Cache, ensuring that even if a record's layout shifts during a schema migration, the application code correctly resolves the intended data by name, not by offset.

The Hazards of Positional Indexing

Relying on positional indexing assumes an immutable schema—a dangerous fallacy in any active project. If a developer inserts a created_at timestamp at index 0 of a PageRecord, every subsequent row[0] access in the CMS engine would suddenly return a timestamp instead of a page_uuid. To prevent this, the bejson_core_get_field_map() helper transforms the static Fields array into a dynamic lookup dictionary. This mapping acts as an abstraction layer between the physical storage structure and the runtime memory representation.

Access Pattern Safety Rating Implications
row[idx] Unsafe Breaks instantly upon any schema alteration. Silent corruption.
row[fmap.get(name)] Safe Schema-agnostic; remains valid even if fields are re-ordered.

Implementing the Field Map Cache

To enforce deterministic execution, NewAgent's codebase is audited for "positional fallbacks." When a library reads an MFDB entity, it must cache the field map. The following pattern demonstrates the mandatory approach for reading a SiteConfig record safely:

# Correct pattern: Resolve indices via Field Map Cache
doc = BEJSONCore.bejson_core_load_file(db_path)
fmap = BEJSONCore.bejson_core_get_field_map(doc)

# Do NOT use hardcoded integers (e.g., row[0])
k_idx = fmap.get("config_key")
v_idx = fmap.get("config_value")

for row in doc.get("Values", []):
    key = row[k_idx]
    value = row[v_idx]
    # ... process safely ...

Deterministic State Recovery

Positional integrity is the backbone of NewAgent's ability to maintain a key_state.bejson or session_resume.json that survives updates. By ensuring that the serialized BEJSON format explicitly defines its Fields schema at the document header, any process loading the file can immediately map the record data to the correct keys. This deterministic approach allows for "Graceful Schema Evolution," where older versions of registry files are read using the old field map, and new entries are added using the updated field map, without ever risking a positional index collision.

This rigor transforms raw disk-based JSON into a predictable, relational database. When combined with atomic write operations, the system guarantees that a system crash during an update cannot result in a partially written or misaligned file structure, as the entire field-to-index integrity is validated before and after every read/write operation.

Chapter 6: Mitigating Hallucinations through Structured Context

Mitigating Hallucinations through Structured Context

Relying on generic system prompts like "you are a helpful, accurate assistant who never lies" is the hallmark of an amateur. Large language models do not hallucinate because they are malicious; they hallucinate because an empty or ambiguous context window forces probabilistic token completion across an ungrounded state space. When an agent loses track of local file layouts, project rules, or available command signatures, it starts inventing plausible-looking garbage. NewAgent eliminates this speculative drift entirely by compiling a strictly deterministic, verified context envelope before every single model turn: the Context Bubble.

Recursive Ancestor Directory Inheritance (context.bejson)

Hardcoding system instructions at the project root fails the moment an agent traverses into nested directories with unique operational constraints. NewAgent implements a hierarchical, directory-level context inheritance engine modeled directly after cascading style inheritance. When a turn executes, the context builder does not just check the current working directory (cwd); it walks upward through the filesystem tree from cwd to the filesystem root, accumulating every encountered context.bejson file.

The resolution engine applies a strict nearest-wins rule: ancestor configurations are loaded first, but if an intermediate or leaf directory specifies an identical section header, the closer file overwrites the ancestral value in place. This prevents rule duplication while allowing sub-modules to dynamically alter their operating parameters.

Filesystem Level Path Example Inherited Sections Precedence Resolution
Catalog (Root) /storage/emulated/0/Admin/dev/ Purpose, Global Rules, Taxonomy Base defaults applied to all child trees.
Project Root .../dev/Python/NewAgent/ Project Rules, Tool Contracts Overrides Global Rules; retains Taxonomy.
Sub-tool Directory .../NewAgent/tools/NA-CMS/ Subsystem Stack, Database Paths Highest priority; merges with Project Rules.

Every context.bejson is formatted strictly under the BEJSON 104a specification, ensuring lightweight, deterministic parsing without structural drift:

{
  "Format": "BEJSON",
  "Format_Version": "104a",
  "Format_Creator": "Elton Boehnen",
  "Records_Type": ["CwdContext"],
  "Fields": [
    {"name": "section", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "content", "type": "string"}
  ],
  "Values": [
    ["Purpose", "Autonomous management and testing of CMS micro-endpoints."],
    ["Rules", "Never run destructive file operations outside tools_lib/na-cms/. Always execute regression tests before emitting completion tags."]
  ]
}

Targeted Knowledge Dripping vs. Context Dilution

Dumping your entire documentation repository into the system prompt guarantees token exhaustion and causes severe attention dilution, increasing model hallucinations. Instead of blasting unneeded technical specs, NewAgent utilizes a keyword-triggered knowledge retrieval subsystem managed by triggers.bejson and knowledge_pool.bejson.

Incoming user messages are scanned for exact and substring keyword matches (e.g., behtml, 104db, mfdb). When a trigger matches, the corresponding technical facts are pulled from the knowledge pool and injected into the turn's prompt payload. Crucially, this mechanism includes:

  • Per-Trigger Cooldown Timers: Prevents the engine from re-injecting 500 lines of unchanged specification every single prompt iteration, preserving the token budget.
  • Deduplication Arrays: When multiple keywords resolve to overlapping technical facts (for example, entering both behtml and z_layer), the resolver normalizes the target references and injects the knowledge block exactly once.
  • Rotating Weighted Pools: Broad architectural facts rotate across turns using round-robin position offsets derived from turn counts, ensuring continuous knowledge exposure without overflowing token thresholds.

Grounding via Explicit Tool-Use Instruction Parsing

The final line of defense against hallucinated execution is grounding model actions in verifiable local state. In naive agent frameworks, models generate continuous prose describing what they would do or fabricating hypothetical terminal outputs. NewAgent's REST engine forbids unchecked stream continuation when actions are declared.

# Execution Loop: Model output is intercepted, executed, and bounded
parsed_actions = actions.parse_actions(response_text)
if parsed_actions:
    # 1. Physical execution against local filesystem and sandboxed subprocesses
    results = await actions.run_action_queue(parsed_actions, ctx)
    exec_results.extend(results)
    
    # 2. Strict XML payload assembly of real outputs, exit codes, and errors
    payload = actions.assemble_results_payload(results)
    
    # 3. Grounded feedback injection: Real command outputs become next turn's user context
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": payload, "_ts": ts})
    logger.log("user_system", payload)

By forcing the model to speak in discrete XML-style action tags (<exec>, <read_file>, <bejson_set_value>), the client halts text streaming, validates paths through bejson_safe_join, checks the shell command against the execution denylist, and executes the physical operation on disk. The actual standard output, standard error, and exit codes are packaged into an explicit results payload and injected back into conversation history. The model never has the opportunity to guess whether a file exists or imagine what a script returned—it is constrained directly by the ground-truth byte output of the host OS.

Chapter 7: Security, Isolation, and Multi-Key Federation

Chapter 7: Security, Isolation, and Multi-Key Federation

When operating autonomous agent runtimes across constrained hardware profiles like Termux on Android or production Linux nodes, security cannot be treated as an afterthought or handled via external monolithic middleware. NewAgent implements a rigorous, defense-in-depth security architecture directly into its core engine libraries. This design guarantees that credentials remain isolated, risky commands are intercepted before execution, local web entry points are cryptographically gated, and multi-node federation operates without exposing raw state.

SHA-256 Hashed API Key Ledger Tracking and Automatic Cooldown

API key exhaustion and rate-limiting (HTTP 429) or invalid authentication errors (HTTP 401/403) are common failure vectors when running high-volume autonomous turns. Naive clients cycle through arrays of plaintext keys blindly, often retrying a exhausted or revoked token in an infinite loop that burns provider quotas and trips account flags. NewAgent replaces plaintext key arrays with a cryptographic tracking ledger. Every API key is indexed and monitored by its full SHA-256 hash stored within persistent registries (config/key_ledger.bejson and config/key_state.bejson).

When an engine encounters a rate limit or authorization failure, the key selection routine (KeyRegistry.next_key()) immediately marks that specific SHA-256 hash as cooling down. Instead of instantly falling back to a doomed token or firing requests into a tight, zero-delay retry loop, the subsystem evaluates failure counts:

  • Immediate Deactivation: Any key flagged as explicitly revoked, suspended, or returning persistent authentication failures is stripped from the active rotation pool instantly.
  • Bounded Backoffing: If all keys enter a cooldown window, the prompter pauses execution for the duration of the soonest-to-expire key's cooldown (capped safely at 30 seconds) rather than hammering the provider API with blind requests.
  • Exponential Backoff with Jitter: Network communication errors trigger randomized exponential backoffs, preventing synchronized request bursts from multi-threaded clients.

Path Guards and Shell Command Denylists

Autonomous agent loops frequently invoke shell commands or manipulate local files based on model responses. Without strict constraints, a model tricked by prompt injection could execute destructive system commands or read sensitive parent directories. NewAgent neutralizes this risk through two mandatory security checkpoints before any action reaches the host operating system.

First, all file operations (read_file, write_file, edit_file, copy_file) must pass through bejson_safe_join. This utility resolves target paths to their canonical absolute forms, aggressively stripping and rejecting any path traversal segments (../) attempting to break out of the designated workspace root.

Second, command execution via do_exec (whether invoked from the REST action queue, the interactions engine, or the web terminal API) passes through a substring-anywhere denylist check (is_command_denylisted()). Dangerous patterns stored in config.json under exec_denylist are intercepted immediately:

# Action Execution Check: Denylist substring matching intercepts dangerous invocations
def is_command_denylisted(command: str, denylist: list[str]) -> bool:
    cmd_lower = command.lower()
    for pattern in denylist:
        if pattern.lower() in cmd_lower:
            return True
    return False

Token-Authenticated Local Web Terminals

The web front end (webagent.py) and job creator (JobMaker.py) expose local HTTP services. To prevent unauthorized cross-origin requests or local network snooping, these services implement strict cryptographic access controls:

  • Loopback Default: Servers bind exclusively to 127.0.0.1 by default. Exposing them externally requires explicit operator flag modification.
  • Shared-Secret Token Authentication: On initial boot, a cryptographically secure web token is auto-generated and persisted to config/config.json (web_auth_token). Every incoming HTTP request must supply this token via the X-Auth-Token header or a query parameter.
  • Constant-Time Comparison: Token verification utilizes secrets.compare_digest() to eliminate timing side-channel attacks.
  • Security Response Headers: All responses include hardened security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Content-Security-Policy, and Strict-Transport-Security) to protect against clickjacking and MIME-type sniffing.

Multi-Node Master-Slave MFDB Federation

In distributed setups where multiple NewAgent instances or secondary agents operate across shared storage or networked environments, Multi-File Database (MFDB) architecture supports a decentralized federation model. Modeled after enterprise HQ-to-satellite synchronization, the database manifest designates a Network_Role parameter (Master or Slave).

Federation Role Operational Behavior Synchronization Direction File Safety Guarantee
Master (HQ) Authoritative coordinator node holding primary entity books. Pushes atomic file replacements down to satellites. Atomic multi-file swap via temporary staging directories.
Slave (Satellite) Edge node executing isolated child operations or sub-agents. Pushes and truncates local execution logs upward. Blind local polling; never exposes unencrypted secrets.
Stand-Alone Default local single-operator instance with no network role. None (fully local filesystem state). Direct file-locking via ResilientPIDLock.

This strict isolation guarantees that even when sub-agents execute parallel workflows or external tools process untrusted web assets, host credentials remain masked, filesystem modifications are strictly bounded by path guards, and state corruption is prevented by atomic BEJSON serialization primitives.

Chapter 8: Companion Tool Suites and Ecosystem Integration

Beyond the core interactive, headless, and web terminal clients, NewAgent's architecture extends outward through a dedicated suite of modular companion tools and administrative frameworks. Located within the project directory structure, these specialized utilities—including NA-CMS, NA-WebToolkit, NA-MD2HTML, and the sub-agent administrative pipeline—do not operate as isolated applications. Instead, they share the exact same vendored core libraries, BEJSON serialization engines, and atomic file-locking mechanisms established by the parent environment.

NA-CMS: Multi-File Database Content Management

The NA-CMS subsystem provides a fully functional content management platform built directly on top of the Multi-File Database (MFDB) and Format 104db relational standard. Rather than depending on heavy external SQL databases or fragile ORM layers, NA-CMS structures its configuration, categories, author profiles, media assets, and published pages into modular entity files governed by strict field maps.

  • Skeleton Loader: Replaces rigid string-concatenation templates with theme-aware HTML skeletons (lib_bejson_NewAgentCMS_cms_skeletons.py). Skeletons are validated against strict {{tag}} contracts prior to site compilation.
  • Draft-to-Promote Workflow: Permits staging edits in isolated draft files (.draft), computing unified diffs against live production templates, and executing atomic promotions backed by automatic history backups.
  • Asset Sanitization & Optimization: Enforces rigorous input scrubbing on uploaded assets, including regex-based SVG script stripping and automatic PIL-based image conversions with transactional verification checks.
NA-CMS Module Core Responsibility Underlying Storage Format
cms_config.py Site configuration and port allocation routing. BEJSON 104db (SiteConfig Entity)
cms_mfdb.py Relational content manager, media ledger, and backup zipper. MFDB Multi-File Manifest & Entity Files
cms_skeletons.py Template rendering, tag validation, and staging pipeline. HTML Skeletons + BEJSON Registry

NA-WebToolkit and Document Conversion

For autonomous web interaction, NA-WebToolkit unifies DuckDuckGo HTML searching, multi-stage webpage extraction, and an interactive mobile terminal browser (MobileBrowserSession). The extraction engine utilizes a resilient fallback cascade (curl → cloudscraper → playwright → requests) with escalating retry delays to prevent aggressive IP blocking. Concurrently, NA-MD2HTML provides an offline, dependency-free Markdown-to-HTML conversion utility featuring recursive indentation-aware list parsing and strict URL scheme allowlisting (_safe_url) to neutralize malicious protocol injections.

Sub-Agent Administrative Framework

The sub-agent subsystem enables NewAgent to dispatch specialized child tasks across durable operational profiles. Managed via subagent_admin.py and powered by lib_bejson_newagent_subagent_runtime.py, sub-agents operate under tightly constrained execution boundaries:

  • Profile Governance: Each sub-agent role is defined by a BEJSON 104 document specifying allowed action tags (allowed_actions), execution denylist overrides, turn caps, and character-budgeted history limits (max_history_chars).
  • Mailbox Signal Exchange: Asynchronous communication between parent and child threads occurs through a persistent signal registry protected by ResilientPIDLock file coordination.
  • Isolated Model Registry: Sub-agents execute against throwaway model scopes (_ScopedModelRegistry), ensuring that profile-specific model overrides never pollute the global runtime configuration.
# Sub-Agent Dispatch Check: Verifying master enablement gate and profile bounds
def dispatch_subagent(subagents_dir: Path, profile_name: str, task: str, cwd: str, config: dict, ...):
    if not config.get("subagents_enabled", False):
        return {"status": "error", "message": "Sub-agent system is globally disabled."}
    profile = profiles.load_profile(subagents_dir, profile_name)
    if not profile:
        return {"status": "error", "message": f"Profile '{profile_name}' not found."}
    # Initialize durable session table row via strict field map
    session_id = sessions.create_session(subagents_dir, profile_name, task, cwd)
    ...

By enforcing modular library reuse, strict schema validation, and atomic storage primitives across every companion tool and ecosystem extension, NewAgent guarantees uniform operational reliability, impenetrable security isolation, and extreme efficiency across its entire feature set.
